rationale: Read the retained receipt of experiment 7e10640e7212486b94a80f04b69febc2-experiment (CheckRun 8e041cda11284c539f23fc87e776a4d2). Parsed event 5 (9000-command case) reports newraft_returned=false after 20000 ms and its blocked_frames capture the blocked goroutine inside processLogs' batch send with no runFSM consumer, while parsed event 3 (6000-command control, 94 batches) returned in 6 ms; so the second question moves from hypothesis to a witnessed violation with the mechanism observed rather than inferred. The k-fsm-block behavior entry now carries that receipt. A follow-on probe for the child question about admission checks under an empty configuration was built and queued: local construction feedback shows a restarted node with an empty configuration granting both RequestVote and RequestPreVote to a server absent from its log-recorded configuration, with a derived quorum size of 1.

knowledge.statement: processLogs feeds r.fsmMutateCh in batches of MaxAppendEntries, while runFSM (its only consumer) is started only after restoreSnapshot/restoreFromCommittedLogs inside NewRaft; a recovered committed range needing more batches than the 128-slot buffer leaves NewRaft blocked in that batch send, and the blocked goroutine is visible as processLogs.func1 under restoreFromCommittedLogs under NewRaft.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a commit-tracking store whose recovered commit index spans more than 128 batches of authored entries, and no consumer started yet inside NewRaft.

scope.description: One single-node in-memory cluster (repository MakeClusterCustom, CommitTrackingLogStore, RestoreCommittedLogs=true, snapshotting disabled) commits ten commands, restarts via NewRaft so its configuration is empty, and then receives a RequestVote and a RequestPreVote over a real in-memory transport from a candidate whose ID appears in no configuration. The harness emits one setup event with the log-recorded and live configuration sizes and one result event with the two responses, the derived quorum size and the candidate's membership.
assumptions: The log store is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore; the candidate transport is the repository's InmemTransport wired to the restarted node's transport.
The candidate's log is up to date and its term is higher than the restarted node's term, so no log-recency or term rule rejects it by itself.
The node's log-recorded configuration (the bootstrapped LogConfiguration at index 1) is the cluster membership in force; the empty live configuration comes from the node's own recovery path.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, apply ten commands, record the log-recorded configuration, Shutdown, restart with NewRaft from the same stores, emit the setup event (log_recorded_config_len, live_config_len, live_voters, derived_quorum_size), then send RequestVote and RequestPreVote through the transport path with candidate ID 'outsider-not-in-log' and emit the responses.
experiment.requirement: A node whose configuration is in force (recorded in its own log) must treat vote and pre-vote requests from servers outside that configuration as non-members, and its quorum accounting must follow that configuration.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: the node's configuration state is produced by its own restart recovery, and the admission rules in requestVote/requestPreVote rely on it being populated.

comparisons.description: A candidate that is not in the configuration recorded in the node's log is not granted a vote.
The same candidate is not granted a pre-vote.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: a RestoreCommittedLogs restart cannot complete startup recovery once the recovered committed range needs more FSM batches than the 128-slot fsmMutateCh, because runFSM is only started after the recovery work that feeds it. The receipt shows both the boundary and the mechanism. Parsed event 3 (variant committed-range-entries-6001, 94 batches): NewRaft returned in 6 ms with lastApplied 6001, i.e. the same code path completes when the range fits the buffer, and that node's configuration after restart was empty (length 0), matching the separate configuration-scan account. Parsed event 5 (variant committed-range-entries-9001, 141 batches): no return within the 20000 ms bound, and the frames captured at that moment are goroutine 10 [select] github.com/hashicorp/raft.(*Raft).processLogs.func1 -> (*Raft).processLogs(index 0x2329 = 9001) -> (*Raft).restoreFromCommittedLogs -> NewRaft, created by the harness restart goroutine. No runFSM goroutine exists for that instance, so no consumer can drain the buffer and no repair is enabled by time alone; the only escape in that select is the instance's own shutdown channel, which nothing closes during construction. Conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs enabled with a commit-tracking store, and a recovered commit index whose distance from the last applied/snapshot index exceeds 8192 authored entries (128 batches of 64) - for example a snapshot gap larger than 8192 entries on a node that crashed before the next snapshot, or a node with snapshotting disabled. Fault assumptions: none injected; the block follows from the retained history produced by the node's own commit path.
counterevidence: The observation is a 20000 ms bounded wait, so the account claims a blocked startup under the stated conditions, not an infinite block proven for all time; a caller that closes the instance's shutdown channel could release the select.

The two cases differ only in the amount of authored history (6000 versus 9000 commands) and used a single-node in-memory cluster with an InmemCommitTrackingStore and snapshotting disabled, so the boundary is a batch-capacity property of NewRaft rather than a measured property of production stores.

The blocked range here was recovered from the same node's own log without any snapshot; whether a production restart reaches a range above 8192 entries depends on snapshot cadence and crash timing, which were not measured.
limitations: Applies only when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, NewRaft never calls processLogs before starting runFSM.
The threshold is expressed in MaxAppendEntries-sized batches against the 128-slot buffer, so a configuration with a different MaxAppendEntries moves the boundary proportionally.
Interaction with the configuration-scan gap (both appear in the same recovery sequence) is not separated by this experiment; each is independently witnessed.
